title: All-hands Oct 2026 - talking points + Q&A (draft)
body:
Purpose:
- Short deck: company updates, product highlights, roadmap signals, and org changes.
- Emphasis: how we’re making inference more predictable and economical for customers (tie to mission).

High-level narrative (3 bullets to lead with):
1) Shipping for production: Dedicated + Private progress - customers moving to predictable, lower-cost footprints. Quick metric: 30% increase in Dedicated trial conversions since July (still confirm exact).
2) Runtime improvements: lower p50 latency for long-context workloads; quantization profiles now live in Optimize beta - saves customers 20-30% per-token costs on average for search/assistant workloads.
3) Developer-first tooling: rollout & tracing improvements (canary/A-B + auto fallback) + new console cost breakdowns. Focus on making customers confident to put mission-critical apps on Redwood.

Announcements to call out (short):
- Private VPC GA (limited regions) - target: next week for procurement pipeline.
- Dedicated capacity: flexible burst pools rolling out to more customers in November.
- Optimize beta: public beta invite list opening this week.
- New SLAs for enterprise contracts (latency and availability tiers).

Talking points for CEO/host (bullet form):
- Thanks - momentum and product-market fit indicators (usage, marquee trials).
- What we shipped (2-3 rapid wins): Private VPC beta -> GA, Dedicated burst pools pilot, Optimize cost-tuning beta.
- Why it matters: inference becomes operationally boring for customers - they get predictable latency and unit economics.
- Roadmap signals (high-level): more automation in routing/fallbacks; better model/regression alerts; expanded regions + compliance work.
- People note: call out SRE/platform hires + kudos to Applied ML team on quantization rollout.

Q&A (draft answers / prep notes) - expect these: 
Q: "What does Private GA mean for existing hosted customers?"
A: Private GA is an option for customers who need networking/data isolation or on-prem. Hosted customers aren’t forced to move; the same API + tooling works across environments. Migration helpers and a support track are available (link to migration playbook).

Q: "How do Dedicated burst pools affect pricing?"
A: Burst pools give predictable extra throughput for high-periods without long-term overcommit. Pricing details: committed monthly baseline + usage-based burst rates. Finance to finalize public pricing by mid-Oct (ENG-3421 tracking).

Q: "Any risk of regressions with Optimize/quantization?"
A: We’re rolling out with quality-monitoring tied to eval sets and canary-on-inference routes; customers can opt into conservative profiles first. Explain tradeoffs (cost vs. quality) and mention automatic rollback if quality drops.

Q: "Are we slowing on new model support?"
A: No - investment in kernel selection and compilation has accelerated onboarding. We have a clear onboarding checklist and automated perf tests for each model variant.

Talking notes (presenter cues / to self):
- Keep examples concrete: show a customer case (anonymized) where Dedicated + caching cut per token cost 35% and improved p95 latency.
- Avoid deep infra details - high-level explanation about smart routing and fallback.
- Call out where to find more info (confluence + docs).

Open items / TODOs before final deck:
- Confirm Dedicated conversion metric with Revenue (Michael) - placeholder number now.
- Get legal sign-off blurb for Private GA (Samira).
- Finalize pricing bullets and publish example pricing table (Finance).
- Add customer quote (ask Solutions Eng for 1-liner).
- Review Q&A with leadership and add any hard questions to the prep doc.

Slack/refs I’ll link in deck notes:
- #product-updates thread from 2026-09-28 (summary)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/784 (canary rollout changes)
- Confluence planning page (linked above)

Presenter rehearsal plan:
- Dry run with execs Thurs 10/08 10:00 - 20-30m.
- Collect hardest Qs and rehearse 2-3 variant answers.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep energy high at top; 2 quick wins -> then roadmap -> people.
- If asked about layoffs / hiring: be transparent - hiring freeze ended for a few teams; we are prioritizing SRE/platform and CS expansion. Keep HR/people-ops in the loop.
- Data points to pull: Dedicated trial conversion %, avg p50/p95 latency improvements, Optimize beta early adopters list.

Rough slide mapping (for deck builder):
1) Title + TL;DR (3 bullets)
2) Company metrics snapshot (usage, revenue signals) - need numbers
3) Product highlights (Private GA, Dedicated burst pools, Optimize beta)
4) How it works (one-slide, customer-friendly: runtime + routing + caching)
5) Customer example + quote
6) Roadmap signals + org asks (hi-level)
7) Q&A prep (top 6 questions)
8) Thank you + ops contact info

If time: planned 45m + 15m Q&A. Keep top 3 priorities to 10 minutes at most.

Last-minute checklist (day of):
- Confirm deck link + access for execs (share with execs list 30m before)
- Mic test / room booking (if in-person)
- Rehearsal with CEO 20m before

-- end draft (will iterate after Michael + Samira feedback)
